name: Oxidative coupling of methane
principle: Methane and oxygen react over a catalyst to give ethylene directly, avoiding steam cracking of ethane or naphtha. Siluria started a demonstration plant at La Porte, Texas, co-located with Braskem America, in about December 2014, and said initial campaigns replicated pilot-scale performance; commercial plants were then planned for 2017 to 2018.

suppliers.name: Siluria Technologies
suppliers.product: OCM demonstration; company bought by McDermott in 2019 and its IP went to Lummus Technology in the 2020 Lummus spin-off

reference_plants.name: Siluria OCM demonstration plant, La Porte, Texas
reference_plants.status: demonstration ran from early 2015 and completed 18 test campaigns in its first year (company release, 11 May 2016); no commercial OCM plant followed — Siluria was bought by McDermott in 2019, and McDermott's 2020 post-bankruptcy spin-off of Lummus Technology included Siluria's intellectual property and the La Porte demonstration plant (read 28 October 2026)

source.note: Siluria Technologies release via PR Newswire, 11 May 2016 (read 28 October 2026); later ownership history from Wikipedia, Siluria Technologies (read 28 October 2026)

advantages: Direct route from natural gas to ethylene (company claim)
limitations: The article gives no capacity or yield

Commercial plants planned for 2017/2018 never materialised; the demonstration ended after the developer was absorbed (McDermott 2019, Lummus Technology spin-off 2020) and no commercial OCM plant has been built
